contested_by: Whether an ice front counts as a sighting of land
notes: The strongest case if an ice front observed from close inshore counts, and no case at all if the definition requires rock. That is a definitional question, not an evidential one, and the row records which definition it answers rather than whether it wins. Dependence on Debenham's 1945 translation is declared rather than the Russian original consulted (ant-gap-bellingshausen-translation): the wording this row and its contest rest on is Debenham's English, and an upgrade to the Russian text is future work, not a precondition for holding this row at contested.

contested_by: Whether what was seen was the mainland peninsula or islands off it
notes: Three days after Bellingshausen and against a different definition, which is why comparing the two dates settles nothing on its own.

contested_by: A sealing log as the record, and a date ten months later than the other two
notes: The weakest of the three on date alone, and the one whose evidence is a commercial document rather than a naval one. Both facts are about the archive, not about what was seen.

asserted_by: Argument from the incentives of the trade
notes: Recorded as a row with no date and no observation, which is the honest shape of an argument from silence. It exists so the contest cannot be presented as a closed field of three.

contested_by: Ross sailing across positions charted as land
notes: A claim to continental extent rather than to a first sighting, which is a different contest and is filed as one. Parts of it survived and parts did not.

contested_by: Overlap in time and place with the United States squadron
notes: Three expeditions on overlapping coast in one season is the best case Act V has, and the essay currently has one of the three charts located.
